question: A hoist report ends with a number found by subtracting a contractual credit of 14 kN from a converted reading. That converted reading is the kilonewton form of the force needed to accelerate a test weight of 9 kg on the hoist's arm. The acceleration in metres per second squared is worked out in stages: start from the smaller of the two values of x for which x^2 - 10x + 16 = 0, add a drive contribution of 15, then add a further gearbox contribution of 3. The hoist's cable is 12 m long, a length that plays no part in the calculation. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?

On a go-kart test track, the kart's acceleration follows a(t) = 5t² + 3t (in m/s², t in seconds) from a standing start; the total speed gained between t = 0 s and t = 1 s, found from the area under this graph, is the kart's speed for the next stage. This speed belongs to an 11 kg battery pack on board. The pack's kinetic energy is converted into kilojoules, then scaled by a factor of 9. The track's total length is 400 m, which plays no role here. Finally, 19 kJ is added. What is the final energy, in kilojoules?
The greatest common divisor of 30 and 317 is 1 m/s. Adding 8 gives 9 m/s. A 21 kg mass has kinetic energy increased by 29, decreased by 18. A pressure is 10 bar. What is the final energy in joules?

The derivative of 2x^3 + x^2 at x = 3 is 63 m/s. A 60 kg mass has kinetic energy converted to kJ, scaled by 8 and 10, increased by 13. A rated speed of 100 m/s is specified. What is the final energy in kJ?

A 75 kg sled on a test track is accelerated at a rate in m/s² found by taking 7 times the sum of 7 and 2, subtracting 20, and then subtracting 2. The booster must supply the thrust needed for this. The track is 450 m long. Five sleds run together, so the combined thrust is 5 times the single-sled value, and the combined thrust is converted to kN. What is the combined thrust, in kN?

A collision impact study calculates velocity as 2 × (8 + 10) - 16 + 23 = 43 m/s. A 2 kg test mass at this velocity yields energy, reduced by 24 J, and converted to kilojoules. The test runs for 15 seconds total. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

A cycle-track laboratory needs the net figure, in kilojoules, for a coasting trial. The trolley's coasting speed v, in m/s, is the smaller value that satisfies v^2 - 7v + 12 = 0. The trolley has a mass of 52000 g, and the energy it carries by virtue of that motion is expressed in kilojoules. A standing rig overhead of 27 kJ is subtracted from that figure. A further instrument allowance of 16 kJ is then subtracted as well. What is the net figure, in kJ?

A lifting mechanism has mass 189 kg and must achieve an acceleration (in m/s²) found by solving x² - 10x + 16 = 0 and taking the smaller root. The resulting force is converted from Newtons to kilonewtons. When 6 such units are chained together and then scaled by 4 for redundancy, and finally increased by 21 kN for operational margin, what is the total lifting force in kiloNewtons? (The system's emergency brake operates at 80 bar pressure.)

Solving x² - 8·x + 12 = 0, larger root is 6 m/s² acceleration. With 199 kg, force = 1194 N, scaled by 12, then 8, increased by 3, scaled by 2. The retention days is 30, not relevant. What is the final force in Newtons?

A haulage report ends with a number that is 5 times a converted total, because 5 depots report together. That converted total is the kilonewton form of a figure obtained by taking a coupling tare of 25 N off a rake total, and the rake total is 5 times the force needed to drive one wagon. Each wagon has a mass of 196000 grams, and its acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 0t accumulates between t = 3 seconds and t = 4 seconds, starting from zero at t = 3 seconds, with t the time in seconds. What number, in kilonewtons, ends the report?

A quadratic solver finds the larger root of x² - 4x + 3 = 0 (which is 3 m/s). A 9 kg mass yields energy, converted to kilojoules, scaled by 10, scaled by 3, and reduced by 25 kJ. What is the final energy in kilojoules?

Right before the lab writes up its energy figure, it always subtracts 4 joules for sensor drift — that's the last correction applied. A pendulum bob used in the experiment has a mass of 46,000 grams, or 46 kilograms. A workshop technician has 16 identical rivets and 117 identical washers left over and wants to sort them into the largest possible number of identical parts kits with nothing left over; that largest number of kits is the starting point of a calculation. To it, the technician adds 3, then adds another 6, and the running total is taken as the bob's speed, in meters per second, at the bottom of its swing. Using that speed and the bob's mass, the bob's kinetic energy is found. The recorded energy is then tripled because three identical pendulums are swung together in the demonstration, and finally, as mentioned at the start, 4 joules is subtracted for drift. The lab bench is 2 meters long. What is the resulting energy, in joules?

Two cycling systems have periods of 16 and 398 time units. Their greatest common divisor establishes a harmonic frequency. This GCD becomes the acceleration in m/s² for a 99 kg element. The resulting force is increased by 25 N from a boost. This adjusted force converts to kilonewtons. Subtracting 12 kN for one load component, then subtracting 15 kN for another, gives the net force. What is the net force in kN? (The system's operating angle is 30 degrees, which is not used.)

A crash-test facility launches a trolley of 47000 grams, and its launch speed in metres per second is 2 times the sum of 7 and 13. The logger records the energy the trolley carries because of its motion and multiplies it by 9, because 9 trolleys go out in a run. The run total is expressed in kilojoules, a standing instrument allowance of 26 kJ is added, and the result is multiplied by 10 for the 10 runs in the programme. The track is 75 m long, a length the logger never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the logger report?

A plant figure is 3 times an adjusted reading, because 3 lines run together. The adjusted reading is a converted force with a contractual credit of 4 kN subtracted from it. That converted force is the kilonewton form of the force needed to drive a slide of 19 kg, with a bearing preload of 9 N added before the conversion. The slide's acceleration in metres per second squared is what the rate curve 4t^2 + 1t accumulates between t = 0 seconds and t = 2 seconds, starting from zero, with t the time in seconds. What is the plant figure, in kilonewtons?

Solving x^2 - 11x + 28 = 0, the larger root (x=7) is picked. A 13 kg object develops kinetic energy. After adding 1, subtracting 14, scaling by 7, and subtracting 25, what is the final energy in joules?

A courier hub has 11 dispatch lanes, and the number of ways of choosing 2 of them, reduced by 7, is used as the speed in m/s of its delivery drones. Each drone has a mass of 40 kg and a rotor span of 1.3 m. A drone's energy of motion at that speed is recorded in kJ. A flight of 10 identical drones has the combined figure, to which the hub adds 15 kJ held in its launch capacitor bank. What total, in kJ, does the hub record?

A thrust calculation begins with 4 times (5 plus 15), yielding acceleration. An engine with mass 30 kilograms responds. Calculate kinetic energy. Scale by 7. Convert to kiloJoules. Subtract 10. Scale by 3. What is the final energy in kiloJoules?

A fleet manager is reporting the total force, in newtons, for 12 identical trucks, less 27 N recovered by a shared regenerative rail. Each truck's figure is the force to accelerate 6 identical 25 000 g crates at once, less 17 N supplied by a tailgate spring. The crates' acceleration, in m/s², is 2 times the sum of 7 and 20. What is the total force, in N?

A drop-tower rig releases a carrier of mass 24 kg. The carrier's release speed in metres per second is read from a calibration chart on which a plotted quantity equals 3 times the cube of the dial setting plus 4 times the square of the dial setting; the speed is the second-order rate of change of that plotted quantity with respect to the dial setting, evaluated at a dial setting of 3. The tower's guide rail is 30 m long. Expressed in kilojoules, the site's energy sheet takes the carrier's kinetic energy, adds 27 kJ for the winch, adds 17 kJ for the compressor, and adds a further 29 kJ for the site cabin. What does the energy sheet total, in kJ?

An oscillation's position function 3x³ - x² has a second derivative (acceleration) at x = 3 seconds of 52 m/s². A 36 kg mass experiences this acceleration for computing energy. The energy is scaled by 12, increased by 27 J, increased by 23 J more, and converted to kilojoules. The oscillation amplitude is 0.5 meters but doesn't factor into energy. What is the final energy in kJ?

A launch bench brings a carriage of 31 kg up to speed along a level rail, and the carriage's acceleration in metres per second squared follows 5t^2 + 7t, with t the time in seconds. Between t = 1 second and t = 3 seconds the speed builds from rest at the start of that interval, and the speed reached at the end is the launch speed. The bench records the energy the carriage carries because of its motion at that speed and expresses it in kilojoules. The converted figure is multiplied by 3 for the 3 carriages in a run, by 7 for the 7 runs in a session, and by 2 for the 2 sessions in the study. The rail is 25 m long, a length the bench never uses. What total, in kilojoules, does the bench report?

A tramway depot tests a car of mass 25000 g on its scale rig. The car's speed, in metres per second, is 4 times a number x, where x is the larger of the two values for which x squared, minus 15 times x, plus 56, equals exactly 0. The depot's inspection pit is 18 m long. The depot's sheet takes the car's kinetic energy in kilojoules and adds 22 kJ drawn by the substation. Ten identical cars run on the line, and the report gives 10 times the single-car figure. What does the report give, in kJ?

A 23000 g test drone flies down a corridor 90 m long at a speed in metres per second equal to the rate of change of the curve 5x^3 + 5x^2 with respect to x at x = 1. Find the drone's kinetic energy in joules at that speed, add 19 J for the energy stored in the spinning rotors, and convert the result to kilojoules. The operator has 11 identical drones, so multiply by 11. From the fleet total subtract 19 kJ for the reserve energy that must stay in the batteries. What is the resulting figure in kJ?
Sum k for k=1 to 4: 1+2+3+4 = 10. With 31 kg, energy = 0.5 × 31 × 10² = 1550 J, convert to 1.55 kJ, minus 5 → -3.45, times 4. The bandwidth is 20 MHz. What is the final energy in kJ?
